info.title: BioAvanceD API
info.description: BioAvanceD backend API (RNF006 C2, #1325). This spec covers only the mounts listed in x-covered-mounts; the rest of the API is not yet documented here. Every response body is JSON with a boolean success; a failure carries error and, often, message. Outside the test environment every route sits behind the global rate limiter and /api/auth also behind the auth limiter, and a request over either limit answers 429.

post.summary: Ingest one record: validate it, then persist it or quarantine it, and audit the outcome (RF029)
post.description: Gates: authenticate, applied to the whole router, and requireRole(3, 4). Every outcome is audited, the refusals included.

entityType.description: The ingestion target. One the ingestion does not support, or one stored outside MongoDB, answers 422.

payload.description: The record, in the target's canonical shape.

provenance.description: The provenance envelope; a missing field quarantines the record.

accessPolicyId.description: ELM-0022: the AccessPolicy ids that govern the record (RF029 AC2). Optional; each must name a policy in force applicable to the entityType, else the record is quarantined.

idempotencyKey.description: A repeated key answers the first call's outcome again.

200.description: An idempotent replay of an accepted record: the first call's result.

201.description: Accepted and persisted, with its outbox event.

403.description: requireRole(3, 4) refused, or error INGESTION_OUT_OF_SCOPE: a field of the record is outside the caller's organization scope.

422.description: error INGESTION_QUARANTINED: the record is quarantined and details lists each violation, also on the replay of a quarantined key; or error INGESTION_TARGET_UNSUPPORTED, INGESTION_STORE_UNSUPPORTED or BARCODE_PERSONAL_DATA.

500.description: error INGESTION_FAILED: an unexpected failure, audited.

503.description: The database is not available, or error CANONICAL_RELEASE_NOT_ACTIVE: the canonical model release in force is absent or not active.

The 201 is a new grant and the 200 an organization already held. The 403 is also an organization outside the caller's. The 404 is a user or an organization not found. The 409 is a target who is an Administrador (global scope) or has no organization-scoped role. The 422 is no organizationId from a global caller (a non-global caller who names none gets 403). The error body is {success, error, message}, with no details.

parameters.description: The user: its _id, id or userID.

409.description: The target is an Administrador or has no organization-scoped role.

422.description: No organizationId was named.

delete.description: Gates: authenticate, requirePermission('updateUser', 'UPDATE'), requirePermission('assignRole', 'UPDATE'), requireOrganizationScope. The 503 comes from authenticate. The 403 is also an organization outside the caller's. The 409 is the user's home organization (changed by PUT /api/users/{id}) or its last organization. An organization the user does not hold answers 200 and changes nothing.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user: its _id, id or userID.

parameters.name: organizationId
parameters.description: The organization to remove.

409.description: The home organization, or the last organization, cannot be removed.

post.summary: Register a participant
post.description: Gates: authenticate, requirePermission('createPatient'), requireOrganizationScope. The 503 comes from authenticate. clinicalUnitId is resolved by the create rule for an organization-scoped caller. The 400 is any untagged failure or a caller of several organizations who names no clinicalUnitId; the 422 carries details.

birthDate.description: Civil identity, stored on the participant identity only. Required; DD/MM/YYYY (day first, read the same way as the duplicate check and search) or an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD).

identityDocument.description: Civil identity document, normalised and checked for a duplicate (a conflict answers 400). Optional.

post.summary: Register a sample
post.description: Gates: authenticate, requirePermission('createSample'), requireOrganizationScope. The 503 comes from authenticate. The 201 is complete; the 202 sets partialSuccess true because the topology integration was queued. The 403 is also STRICT_MODE_BLOCKED. The 404 is an organizationId a global caller names that does not exist. The 422 is a qualificationContext error, a field of the RCS result (RCS_DERIVED_WRITE_REFUSED with fields), or a 422-tagged failure and carries details; every other failure is 400.

boxId.description: The storage box (an object id); required.

positionCode.description: The position in the box; required.

specimenId.description: Generated when omitted; an existing one is refused.

specimenStatus.description: closed cannot be assigned at registration.

organizationId.description: Resolved by the create rule; never stored from the body as such.

qualificationContext.description: The use context checked by RF018 AC2.

governanceEvidence.description: RNF018 AC5: governance evidence references, read when the body carries sprec, in the shape POST /api/quality/preview takes (optional arrays traceability, monitoring and documentation, at most 20 each, of { uri, hash }). Each presented reference is resolved against the stored record before certification; one with a missing hash, an unresolvable URI or a different stored hash fails its category's governance rule. A custody-event reference cannot resolve at registration, since the sample does not exist yet. A documentation reference resolves only to an approval of the sample's collectionId. Absent evidence leaves its criterion unread. A governanceEvidenceResolution the body sends is ignored.

202.description: The sample was registered and its topology integration queued.

post.description: Gates: authenticate, requirePermission('withdrawSample', 'UPDATE'), requireOrganizationScope. The 503 comes from authenticate. The 403 is also a sample of another organization. The 400 is a missing sampleID, a consent refusal, or any failure of the withdrawal.

post.summary: Register a participant
post.description: Gates: authenticate, requirePermission('createPatient'), requireOrganizationScope. The 503 comes from authenticate and from the handler. The body is checked against the canonical fields first (a field outside them answers 422); the participantId is replaced by a generated one, the status is set to PENDING_CONSENT and the consent notification is queued. The 201 returns only the participantId. An organization-scoped caller registers into its own organization (a caller of several who names none in clinicalUnitId answers 400). The 400 is also a missing patientName, birthDate or consentTemplateId, an invalid consentTemplateId, and a deceased participant without the complete representative. The 409 is an identityDocument, recordNumber, phone, or name and birth date already registered. The 422 is a non-canonical field, a validation failure (details: a missing participantId or sex, an invalid email or representative email) or a study that is not active. A consentTemplateId or studyId that does not exist answers 500 (there is no 404).

post.summary: Register a sample
post.description: Gates: authenticate, requirePermission('createSample'), requireOrganizationScope, then the payload validation. The 503 comes from authenticate and from the handler. The 422 comes first from the payload validation (a prohibited legacy field such as patientID or sampleID, a field of the RCS result as RCS_DERIVED_WRITE_REFUSED with fields, or a failed field check, with details) and then from the registration (a study or protocol that is not active or approved). The 403 is also STRICT_MODE_BLOCKED. The 404 is a participant, study, protocol, collection, collection site or parent sample that does not exist. The 409 is a storage position that is taken. The 201 is complete; the 202 sets partialSuccess true because the topology integration was queued. Any other failure that names a missing or invalid field answers 400, and the rest 500.

Each presented reference is resolved against the stored record before certification; one with a missing hash, an unresolvable URI or a different stored hash fails its category's governance rule. A custody-event reference cannot resolve at registration, since the sample does not exist yet. A documentation reference resolves only to an approval of the sample's collectionId. Absent evidence leaves its criterion unread. A governanceEvidenceResolution the body sends is ignored.

put.description: Gates: authenticate, requirePermission('editSample'), requireOrganizationScope. The 503 comes from authenticate and from the handler. A sample of another organization answers 403. The 403 is also a move of a sample that has no organizationId to a collectionSite outside the caller's. The 404 is an unknown sample. The 409 is a quarantined sample set to available (QUARANTINE_RELEASE_REQUIRED: use POST /api/samples/{id}/quarantine/release). The 422 is a refused status write (SPECIMEN_STATUS_WRITE_REFUSED: quantityStatus, closed, an invalid or v1.3.0 status, or any change out of closed) or a barcode write after the migration window (LEGACY_BARCODE_WRITE_REFUSED), or a write to the RCS result (RCS_DERIVED_WRITE_REFUSED: biologicalPenalty, rcsScore, scoreBasedGrade, finalGrade, gradeRoute, axisPenalties, calculationTrace, rcsEvaluation, modelVersion, matrixType, governanceStatus, governanceFailureReasons, governanceRuleCodes or sealedRcsAssessmentId, set only by RCS certification, with fields and details), or a negative or non-numeric quantity, currentQuantity or initialQuantity (INVALID_QUANTITY, with fields and details). The 422 is also a sprec that differs from the stored one (SPREC_WRITE_REFUSED, with fields and details): the SPREC is the certified input and an edit does not change it, so a body repeating the stored sprec passes and writes nothing. Every other failure answers 400. Only the listed fields are written; any other body field is ignored. The 200 returns the stored sample.

The 400 is a missing file or one the parser refuses (format, MIME type, size over 100 MB, content that does not match its extension), an invalid file type or fileRole, and any other failure. A result whose sample is in another organization answers 403; for a caller whose scope is not global, so does a result whose sample no longer exists. An {id} that is not an object id answers 500. The route has no 400 and no 422.

put.description: Gates: authenticate, requirePermission('editResult'), requireOrganizationScope. The 503 comes from authenticate. A result whose sample is in another organization answers 403; for a caller whose scope is not global, so does a result whose sample no longer exists. The 400 is an {id} that is not an object id and any other failure. Only the listed fields are written; specimenId is changed by PUT /api/results/{id}/link-sample, and any other body field is ignored. The 200 carries no data. The route has no 422.

delete.description: Gates: authenticate, requirePermission('deleteResult'), requireOrganizationScope. The 503 comes from authenticate. A result whose sample is in another organization answers 403; for a caller whose scope is not global, so does a result whose sample no longer exists. The result record is removed; the file is not. The 400 is an {id} that is not an object id and any other failure. The route has no 422.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The result: its _id (an object id); anything else is a failure of the handler.

get.description: Gates: authenticate, requireOrganizationScope. The 503 comes from authenticate. A result whose sample is in another organization answers 403; for a caller whose scope is not global, so does a result whose sample no longer exists. The 200 is the file as an attachment, or, when the record holds an http URL, a JSON body {redirect: true, url} with no success field. The 404 is an unknown result or a file missing on disk. put.summary: Link an analysis result to a sample
put.description: Gates: authenticate, requirePermission('editResult'), requireOrganizationScope. The 503 comes from authenticate. A result whose sample is in another organization answers 403; for a caller whose scope is not global, so does a result whose sample no longer exists. The destination sample must be in the caller's organizations too (403). The 400 is a missing specimenId, an {id} that is not an object id, and any other failure. The 404 is an unknown result or an unknown sample. The route has no 422.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The result: its _id (an object id); anything else is a failure of the handler.

get.description: Gates: authenticate, requirePermission('viewReports'). The 503 comes from authenticate and from the handler. The 403 is also a caller with no usable organization: this router resolves the scope in the handler, there is no requireOrganizationScope gate. A caller of one or more organizations lists the reports stamped with one of them (a report with no organization is reached by global scope only); an external user lists only the reports a grant names. The 200 is a bare array with no success field, newest first. The route has no 400, 404 or 422.

Gates: authenticate, requirePermission('viewReports'). The 503 comes from authenticate and from the handler. The 403 is also a caller with no usable organization: this router resolves the scope in the handler, there is no requireOrganizationScope gate. The 403 is also a report of another organization (a report with no organization is reached by global scope only) and, for an external user, a report no grant names. The 200 is the report itself with no success field. The 404 is an unknown id. The route has no 400 and no 422.

parameters.description: The report: its numeric reportID, or its 24-character _id.

delete.description: Gates: authenticate, requirePermission('viewReports'), requireRole(3, 4). The 503 comes from authenticate and from the handler. The 403 is a caller whose hierarchy level is not 3 or 4 (Coordenador or Administrador), a caller with no usable organization and a report of another organization (a report with no organization is reached by global scope only); the report grant of an external user is not consulted. The 404 is an unknown id, or a report that was removed between the lookup and the delete. The route has no 400 and no 422.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The report: its numeric reportID, or its 24-character _id.

post.summary: Generate and save a report
post.description: Gates: authenticate, requirePermission('viewReports'). The 503 comes from authenticate and from the handler. The report is built from the same preview data as POST /api/reports/{type}/preview, stored in reportData as JSON text and stamped with the organizations of the caller (none for a global caller). The 403 is also a report type that reads the audit trail (accessLogs, auditEvents) asked by a caller who is neither an administrator nor an auditor, a type that an external user's report grant does not name, and a type scoped by organization asked by a caller with no usable organization; the preview data is bounded by the type's export allow-list. An unknown or retired {type} is not an error here: the preview data is {total: 0, message, type}. The 400 is a missing reportType. The 201 is the report itself with no success field. The route has no 404 and no 422.

post.summary: Create a report template
post.description: Gates: authenticate (router-wide), requirePermission('manageReportTemplates'). The 503 comes from authenticate and from the handler. The 201 is the new template, always with isSystemDefined false and createdBy set from the caller. The 409 is a code already held by another template. The 422 is a missing code, name or handlerKey, a code that does not match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$ once lower-cased, an unknown handlerKey or an unknown templateStatus (details lists each reason). The route has no 400 and no 404.

templateStatus.description: Defaults to active; a retired template no longer resolves as a report type.

updatedBy.description: Read by the model and stored as sent.

createdAt.description: Read by the model and stored as sent, else the creation time.

409.description: The code is already held by another template.

put.description: Gates: authenticate (router-wide), requirePermission('manageReportTemplates'). The 503 comes from authenticate and from the handler. The body is merged over the stored template and the merge is validated, so every field is optional and a body without name or handlerKey keeps the stored ones; the code cannot change (a code in the body is ignored) and isSystemDefined is not read. System templates can be edited. The 404 is an unknown id or code. The 422 is a merged template with an empty name, an unknown handlerKey or an unknown templateStatus (details lists each reason). The route has no 400.

post.summary: Stage a batch import file
post.description: Gates: authenticate, requirePermission('uploadFiles'), requireOrganizationScope, the multipart parser for the file field named file. The 503 comes from authenticate and from the handler. The organization is resolved before anything is staged and is stamped on the batch. The organization is resolved from the caller: a caller of one organization uses it, a caller of several must name organizationId (400 otherwise), a global caller may name any registered one (404 when it is unknown) or none. The 202 means the file is queued for staging, not imported; follow it with GET /api/import/batch/{jobId}. The 400 is a missing file, a file the parser refuses, and a caller of several organizations who names none. The 403 is also a caller with no organization. The 404 is an unknown organizationId. The route has no 422. A refusal of the multipart parser is not caught and answers through the default error handler, not as JSON: a file with an .exe, .sh or .bat extension or a MIME type outside CSV, plain text, Excel (xls, xlsx) and JSON answers 400, a file over 100 MB or an unexpected file field answers 500.

post.summary: Stage an FHIR Bundle
post.description: Gates: authenticate, requirePermission('uploadFiles'), requireOrganizationScope, the multipart parser for the file field named file. The 503 comes from authenticate. The Bundle is the uploaded JSON file or, when there is no file, the JSON request body itself (resourceType Bundle with an entry array holding at least one Specimen); the batch is stamped with the caller's organization. The organization is resolved from the caller: a caller of one organization uses it, a caller of several must name organizationId (400 otherwise), a global caller may name any registered one (404 when it is unknown) or none. The 201 is the staged batch and its records. The 400 is a file that is not JSON, a body that is not a Bundle with an entry array, a Bundle without a Specimen, and a caller of several organizations who names none; the body of an error has success and message, with no error field. The 403 is also a caller with no organization. The 404 is an unknown organizationId. The parser has no file filter and a 20 MB limit: a larger file is not caught and answers 500 through the default error handler, not as JSON. The route has no 422.

post.summary: Import a file synchronously
post.description: Gates: authenticate, requirePermission('uploadFiles'), requireOrganizationScope, the multipart parser for the file field named file. The 503 comes from authenticate and from the handler. The file is imported before the response. The 200 reports success counts in data; rows that failed are listed in data.errors and the call still answers 200. dataType patients, samples and temperature import; samples resolve the organization from the caller. The organization is resolved from the caller: a caller of one organization uses it, a caller of several must name organizationId (400 otherwise), a global caller may name any registered one (404 when it is unknown) or none. A dataType of results is not implemented: it answers 200 with data {success: 0, total: 0} and one error entry. A dataType of locations answers 400 (the legacy collection is read-only). A missing or unknown dataType, and any failure of the import, answer 500. The 400 is a missing file, a file the parser refuses, a locations import and, for samples, a caller of several organizations who names none. The 403 is also a caller with no organization, for samples. The 404 is an unknown organizationId, for samples. The route has no 422. A refusal of the multipart parser is not caught and answers through the default error handler, not as JSON: a file with an .exe, .sh or .bat extension or a MIME type outside CSV, Excel (xls), JSON and ZIP (an xlsx file is refused) answers 400, a file over 100 MB or an unexpected file field answers 500.

post.description: Gates: authenticate, requireRole(3, 4) (Coordenador or Administrador), requireOrganizationScope. The body is validated first, so every missing or malformed field answers 422 VALIDATION_ERROR (details lists each reason) before any 403 or 404. Exactly one of dispositionActionId and accessRequestId must be a non-blank string: both or neither answer 422, and an empty string counts as not sent (a whitespace-only dispositionActionId passes this check but is still looked up, and answers 404 AUTHORIZATION_NOT_FOUND). Then: 403 OUT_OF_SCOPE when the sender organization is outside the caller's scope; 422 ORGANIZATION_NOT_FOUND when the sender or recipient is unknown; 404 AUTHORIZATION_NOT_FOUND; 422 AUTHORIZATION_NOT_TRANSFER (the disposition action is not a transfer of specimens); 409 AUTHORIZATION_NOT_EXECUTED (transfer not executed) or AUTHORIZATION_NOT_RELEASED (distribution not released); 422 SPECIMEN_NOT_FOUND or SPECIMEN_NOT_AUTHORIZED. The dispatch is audited. The 503 comes from authenticate and from the handler. The 500 is also a failure of the dispatch. The route has no 400 (#660).

post.description: Gates: authenticate, requireRole(3, 4) (Coordenador or Administrador), requireOrganizationScope. The checks run in this order: 404 SHIPMENT_NOT_FOUND; 403 OUT_OF_SCOPE (the recipient organization is outside the caller's scope); 409 ALREADY_RECEIVED; then the body, 422 VALIDATION_ERROR (details lists each reason) for a missing or invalid receiptDateTime, one before the dispatch, or a conditionOnReceipt that is not an object or has a key other than integrity, temperature, packaging and discrepancies; then 409 CONCURRENT_UPDATE when the shipment changed meanwhile. So a missing receiptDateTime is answered 422 only after the 404, 403 and 409 checks. The receipt is audited. The 503 comes from authenticate and from the handler. The route has no 400.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The shipmentId (a UUID).

receiptDateTime.description: ISO 8601, not before the shipment's dispatchDateTime.

conditionOnReceipt.description: Integrity, temperature, packaging and discrepancies on arrival (ELM-0407); no other key.

404.description: SHIPMENT_NOT_FOUND.

409.description: ALREADY_RECEIVED (the receipt was recorded before) or CONCURRENT_UPDATE (the shipment changed meanwhile; read it again).

get.summary: Download a file by its access token
get.description: Gates: none. No authenticate, so it never answers 401 and never 400: the token query parameter is the credential (RNF029 C5, #1321), a short-lived token the download handlers issue for one file. An expired token answers 403 with code FILE_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRED; a missing, tampered or superseded token (the file's stored object changed since the token was issued) answers 403 with FILE_ACCESS_TOKEN_INVALID. Each refusal is audited. 404 is a deleted or unknown file row, or bytes missing in storage. 500 is a failure reading or decrypting the stored object, or any other failure. 503 is no database. The 200 is the file's bytes (decrypted when stored encrypted), not JSON, with Content-Disposition and Cache-Control: no-store.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The file access token. A request without it is refused with 403 FILE_ACCESS_TOKEN_INVALID.

403.description: The token is expired (code FILE_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRED), or missing, tampered or superseded (code FILE_ACCESS_TOKEN_INVALID).

404.description: The file row is deleted or unknown, or its bytes are missing in storage.

post.summary: Preview the quality assessment of a sample payload
post.description: Gates: authenticate. Evaluates the quality of the posted sample without storing anything; no body field is required and any body is assessed. The 500 is only authenticate's (or an unexpected throw in the evidence lookup or the evaluation); the 503 is authenticate's.

schema.description: The sample fields to assess; legacy quality fields are normalized to the canonical ones. Optional governanceEvidence (RNF018 AC5): an object with optional arrays traceability, monitoring and documentation (at most 20 each) of { uri, hash }, where uri is urn:bioavanced:custody-event:<eventId>, urn:bioavanced:telemetry-exposure-summary:<id> or urn:bioavanced:collection-governance-approval:<approvalId> respectively, and hash is sha256:<64 lower-case hex> of the stored record. Optional specimenId names the specimen a custody event or telemetry summary must belong to. Optional collectionId names the collection a collection-governance-approval reference must belong to: documentation evidence, an SOP's included, is an approval of that collection, and one of another collection, or with no collectionId, is an unresolvable URI. Each presented reference is resolved against the stored record before certification; one with a missing hash, an unresolvable URI or a different stored hash fails its category's governance rule. A governanceEvidenceResolution the client sends is ignored.

data.description: The certification result, with rcs_input, deprecated_legacy_fields, governance_evidence and, when the payload carried one, qualification_context. governance_evidence holds the six governance criteria (metadataComplete, terminologyValid, traceabilityOk, monitoringOk, documentationOk, semanticCompatible), each true, false or null, with unresolvedReasons, gateResult ('pass', 'fail' or null), failureReasons, evidenceRefs (the URIs of the references that resolved) and the validation rule set's version and checksum; traceabilityOk, monitoringOk and documentationOk are true only when governanceEvidence references of that category were presented and all resolved; semanticCompatible is true only when every axis of the matrix resolved its code and context and the traceability (custody) references resolved, and gateResult is 'pass' when all six criteria are true.

get.summary: Check that a sample can receive an analysis file
get.description: Gates: authenticate; no organization scope. 404 is any eligibility failure (an unknown or ambiguous sample, a sample without a participant, an unknown participant, a consent without an acceptance date, or a database failure, which the service reports as a failure too) except a patient whose status is exactly PENDING_CONSENT, which is 409. The body's code is CONSENT_PENDING whenever the failure carries a patient status (so a 404 can carry CONSENT_PENDING, for a status other than ACCEPTED_CONSENT that is not PENDING_CONSENT), otherwise SAMPLE_NOT_FOUND. The handler sends no 500 of its own; the 500 is authenticate's. Compare POST /api/analysis-files/upload, which answers 400 where this answers 404.

parameters.name: sampleIdentifier
parameters.description: The sample: its _id, specimenId or barcode.

404.description: The sample is not eligible (code SAMPLE_NOT_FOUND, or CONSENT_PENDING when the failure carries a patient status other than PENDING_CONSENT).

409.description: The patient's status is PENDING_CONSENT (code CONSENT_PENDING).

post.summary: Upload an analysis file to a sample
post.description: Gates: authenticate, then the multipart parser for the file field named file (at most 500 MB), then a check that the file's leading bytes match its extension (RF007 AC1, RNF029 C1, #1321); no organization scope. A parser error (a blocked or disallowed extension or MIME type, a file over 500 MB) goes to Express's default error handler, which answers 500 (the app registers no error handler of its own), not 400. A file whose content does not match its extension answers 400 (Invalid file content). The handler answers 503 with no database; 400 with no file, or with no specimenId; 409 (code CONSENT_PENDING) when the sample's patient has any status other than ACCEPTED_CONSENT; 400 (code SAMPLE_NOT_FOUND) for any other eligibility failure; 201 on success. The handler's catch answers 400 (not 500) for any other failure. Compare GET /api/analysis-files/validate/{sampleIdentifier}, which answers 404 for the same failure and 409 only for PENDING_CONSENT.

file.description: The analysis file, at most 500 MB, with an allowed extension and MIME type and leading bytes that match the extension.

specimenId.description: The sample: its _id, specimenId or barcode.

400.description: No file, no specimenId, content that does not match the extension (Invalid file content), an unknown or ineligible sample (code SAMPLE_NOT_FOUND), or any other failure of the handler.

409.description: The patient's status is not ACCEPTED_CONSENT (code CONSENT_PENDING).

500.description: A parser error (blocked or disallowed type, file over 500 MB) answered by the default error handler, or authenticate's failure.

get.description: Gates: authenticate. Returns the active types sorted by name. The 503 comes from authenticate and from the handler (no database); the 500 is also a failure of the read.

post.summary: Create an analysis type
post.description: Gates: authenticate, requireRole(4) (Administrador). The code defaults to the slug of name and is lower-cased. The 422 (error "Dados inválidos", details a list of reasons) is a name that is not a non-empty string, or a resulting code that is empty or not a string (a name whose slug is empty answers 422). The 409 is a code that already exists. The handler's catch answers 400 (not 500) when the insert fails; the 500 comes from the gates. The 503 comes from authenticate and from the handler (no database).

code.description: Defaults to the slug of name; stored lower-cased.

400.description: The insert failed.

409.description: The code already exists.

post.summary: Register a DiagnosticReport
post.description: Gates: authenticate, requirePermission('createPatient'), requireOrganizationScope (P1X-0168..0174, #695). Only participantId, encounterId, reportStatus, issuedDateTime, resultIds and documentUri are read; diagnosticReportId is always assigned. The order is: 503 with no database; 422 for a shape error (resultIds not a list, reportStatus not a string, issuedDateTime not a date); then 403 when a non-blank participantId names a patient outside the caller's organization scope (an unknown patient is not refused); then 422 for a blank participantId or reportStatus; then 422 for a resultIds entry that is no ClinicalObservation; 201. So a missing reportStatus beside an out-of-scope participantId answers 403, not 422. Any other failure answers 500.

resultIds.description: Each entry must be an existing ClinicalObservation.

403.description: The participant's patient record lies outside the caller's organization scope (Acesso negado), or a gate refused (no organization assigned, missing permission, or authenticate's 403).

get.description: Gates: authenticate, requireOrganizationScope. The list is per participant: the participantId query parameter is required and a blank one answers 400 (the only 400 among the diagnostic report routes). 403 when the participant's patient record lies outside the caller's organization scope. 503 comes from the gates and from the handler (no database).

parameters.name: participantId
parameters.description: The participant whose reports are listed.

400.description: participantId is missing or blank.

403.description: The participant's patient record lies outside the caller's organization scope (Acesso negado), or a gate refused (no organization assigned, missing permission, or authenticate's 403).

get.description: Gates: authenticate, requireOrganizationScope. The path value is the report's own diagnosticReportId (uuid), not the _id. 404 (Registro não encontrado) comes first, then 403 when the report's participant lies outside the caller's organization scope. The route has no 400. 503 comes from the gates and from the handler (no database).

parameters.name: diagnosticReportId
parameters.description: The report's diagnosticReportId (uuid), not its _id.

403.description: The participant's patient record lies outside the caller's organization scope (Acesso negado), or a gate refused (no organization assigned, missing permission, or authenticate's 403).

post.summary: Probe the ingestion gateway
post.description: Gates: requireTestSupportSecret (header x-test-support-secret). No authenticate, so it never answers 401. Runs the real ingestion gateway on the posted record and audits the attempt (RF029, #669). Registered only when NODE_ENV is not production and ENABLE_TEST_SUPPORT_ROUTES is true (#675); otherwise the route does not exist. A wrong or missing secret answers 403. 503 is no database. Every error of the gateway is a 500 (it sets no status code), including a missing entityType. The 200 carries status accepted, quarantined, or idempotent_replay (the replay of an idempotencyKey already claimed).

403.description: The secret is wrong or missing (Não autorizado).

500.description: The gateway failed, including a missing entityType.

post.summary: Run the Foundation job on an e2e_foundation_ scratch database
post.description: Gates: requireTestSupportSecret (header x-test-support-secret). No authenticate, so it never answers 401. Registered only when NODE_ENV is not production and ENABLE_TEST_SUPPORT_ROUTES is true (#675); otherwise the route does not exist. Runs the Foundation job's own runSeed() in the posted mode against the posted scratch database on the same Mongo server, never the stack's own database, so a rollback or a failing gate leaves the stack's FoundationDataRun and ReadinessReport untouched (RF022, RNF031, #1485). A wrong or missing secret answers 403. 400 is a database outside the e2e_foundation_ namespace (invalid_database) or a mode the job does not run (invalid_mode); validation runs before any database access. 503 is no database or a database named as the stack's own; 500 is any failure of the job.

200.description: The FoundationDataRun, its ReadinessReport (null for a dry run) and the job's exit code.

400.description: invalid_database or invalid_mode.

403.description: The secret is wrong or missing (Não autorizado).

500.description: The Foundation job failed.

post.summary: Run the graph projection reconciliation scoped to named samples
post.description: Gates: requireTestSupportSecret (header x-test-support-secret). No authenticate, so it never answers 401. Registered only when NODE_ENV is not production and ENABLE_TEST_SUPPORT_ROUTES is true (#675); otherwise the route does not exist. Runs the reconciliation script's own reconcile() scoped to the posted specimenIds, never over the whole database: it reports the named samples with no Sample node or a drifted one, and the named samples' stalled outbox aggregates; with repair it requeues their dead letters and appends their events to the outbox again. The graph is only read (RF023 AC6, RNF016 C2, RNF019 C6 C7, #1502). A wrong or missing secret answers 403. 400 is a specimenIds that is not a list of 1 to 50 24-hex ids (invalid_specimen_ids) or a repair that is not a boolean (invalid_repair); validation runs before any database access. 503 is no database or no Neo4j driver; 500 is any failure of the reconciliation.

200.description: The reconciliation result: the stalled aggregates, the samples missing from or drifted from the graph, and what the repair requeued or appended.

400.description: invalid_specimen_ids or invalid_repair.

403.description: The secret is wrong or missing (Não autorizado).

500.description: The reconciliation failed.

post.summary: Run a reference import into an E2E_ dataset
post.description: Gates: requireTestSupportSecret (header x-test-support-secret). No authenticate, so it never answers 401. Registered only when NODE_ENV is not production and ENABLE_TEST_SUPPORT_ROUTES is true (#675); otherwise the route does not exist. Writes the posted records as a JSONL file and runs the real reference import pipeline on it with the HPO source's registration and normalizer, under the posted E2E_ datasetCode and its own systemUri urn:bioavanced:e2e:<datasetCode>, so no real dataset is touched (RF028, RNF032, #1476). The release it registers waits approved for an explicit promotion. A wrong or missing secret answers 403. 400 is a datasetCode outside the E2E_ namespace (invalid_dataset_code), a bad datasetVersion (invalid_dataset_version) or records that are not 1..1000 objects (invalid_records); validation runs before any file or database access. 503 is no database; 500 is any failure of the import.

200.description: The import run, its release and whether it was approved.

400.description: invalid_dataset_code, invalid_dataset_version or invalid_records.

403.description: The secret is wrong or missing (Não autorizado).

500.description: The import failed.

post.summary: Check the preserved asset of an E2E_ reference release
post.description: Gates: requireTestSupportSecret (header x-test-support-secret). No authenticate, so it never answers 401. Registered only when NODE_ENV is not production and ENABLE_TEST_SUPPORT_ROUTES is true (#675); otherwise the route does not exist. Reads the object storage copy a reference import preserved for an E2E_ datasetCode and checksum, and answers whether it exists and the sha256 of its stored bytes (RF028 AC2, RNF032, #1476). It reads no database. A wrong or missing secret answers 403. 400 is a datasetCode outside the E2E_ namespace (invalid_dataset_code) or a checksum that is not 64 lowercase hex digits (invalid_checksum). A missing object, or one that is not a regular file, is a 200 with exists false and sha256 null. 500 is any other failure of the read.

200.description: Whether the preserved asset exists, and the sha256 of its stored bytes.

400.description: invalid_dataset_code or invalid_checksum.

403.description: The secret is wrong or missing (Não autorizado).

500.description: The read of the stored object failed.

get.description: Gates: authenticate. Returns the collection's regime and governance context, its approvals (newest createdAt first) and its events (oldest first). The 404 is an unknown collection. The 503 comes from authenticate and from the handler. The 401 and 403 come from the gate. The route has no 400, 409 or 422. The 500 is also a failure of the read.

post.summary: Register an approval of a collection
post.description: Gates: authenticate, requireRole(3, 4) (Coordenador, Administrador). Stores a governance approval for the collection; the collectionId is the path's whatever the body names, and an approvalId or statusHistory in the body is discarded (a UUID is generated, the history starts empty). The 404 is an unknown collection. The 422 (error is the message, details a list of reasons) is a body the model refuses: an authority that is not a non-empty string, a caae that is present and not a non-empty string, a documentUri that is not a URI, a documentChecksum that is not a SHA-256, an effectivePeriod without a valid start or with an end before it, a status outside draft, active, suspended and revoked, or a responsibleOrganizationId that is not a non-empty string; or a responsibleOrganizationId that names no stored organization. The route has no 409. The 401, 403 and 503 come from the gates and from the handler. The 500 is also a failure of the write or of its audit entry.

post.summary: Change the status of an approval of a collection
post.description: Gates: authenticate, requireRole(3, 4) (Coordenador, Administrador). Moves the approval along draft to active or revoked, active to suspended or revoked, suspended to active or revoked; revoked is final. A history entry records the change. The 404 is an approval of that collection that is not stored (the collection itself is not looked up). The 422 (error is the message, details a list) is a status that is missing or not an allowed move from the current one. The 409 is an approval that changed state while the move was being made. The 401, 403 and 503 come from the gates and from the handler. The 500 is also a failure of the write or of its audit entry.

post.summary: Record a governance decision of a collection
post.description: Gates: authenticate, requireRole(3, 4) (Coordenador, Administrador). The one writer of a collection's regime and governance context (RF020 AC4). The first context is a created decision; a newRegime different from the stored one is a regime_change, with the new regime's context. A collection that already has a context answers 422 for a created decision. Each names a justification and at least one approval of this collection that is active and inside its effective period; for a biorepository the context's ethicsApprovalId is added to approvalIds. The 404 is an unknown collection. The 422 (error is the message, details a list where there are several) is a newRegime outside biobank and biorepository, a context the regime refuses (missing or foreign fields), a reference that names no stored study, protocol, organization, access policy or ethics approval of the collection, a protocolVersion that differs from the protocol's, an event the model refuses (no approval, no justification), or an approval that is missing or not in force. The 409 is a collection whose governance changed while the decision was being recorded. The 401, 403 and 503 come from the gates and from the handler. The 500 is also a failure of the write or of its audit entry.

parameters.description: The collection: its collectionId (an _id is not matched).

newRegime.description: The regime to set; the stored regime when absent, which must then be one of the two.

governanceContext.description: Required. For biorepository: studyId, protocolId, protocolVersion, caae, responsibleOrganizationId, responsibleInvestigatorId, ethicsApprovalId (an approval of this collection), validityPeriod { start, end? } and plannedEndDate or closureCondition. For biobank: broadPurpose, governancePolicyId, accessCommitteeId, institutionalCustodianId, futureUseConditions (non-empty list), applicableConsentModel (a non-empty list of specific, broad, tiered or dynamic) and newEthicsReviewRule (always or when_required_by_policy). The other regime's fields are refused.

approvalIds.description: The approvals of this collection the decision rests on; at least one is needed, counting the ethics approval of a biorepository context.

201.description: The decision is recorded; data holds the event and the collection's new regime and context.

404.description: collectionId names no stored collection.

409.description: The governance of the collection changed during the operation; try again.

post.description: Gates: authenticate, requireRole(3, 4) (Coordenador, Administrador). Stores the fields the model keeps, never the whole body; biobankId is the body's, else a generated UUID. The 422 (error "Payload inválido", details a list of reasons) is a body the model refuses: a biobankName, biobankDescription, legalEntityId or biobankStatus that is not a non-empty string, a countryCode that is missing or not ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, a contactInformation without a filled contact, an infrastructureCapabilities, bioprocessingCapabilities, qualityManagementStandards, infrastructuralCapabilities, organisationalCapabilities or bioprocessingAnalyticalCapabilities that is not a list, a code list holding an empty or non-string code, or a url that is not a URI. The 404 is checked after the 422: legalEntityId names no organization (the organizationId is looked up in organizations). The 401, 403 and 503 come from the gates. The 500 is also a failure of the write.

post.summary: Register a sample and its participant through the intake wizard
post.description: Gates: authenticate, requirePermission('createSample'), requireOrganizationScope, then intakeGovernanceResponseGuard, which rebuilds a body whose success is true as the 200 below (its governance status read back from the stored sample) and passes any other body through unchanged. It matches the participant or creates one (a match outside the caller's organizations is linked, never updated), decides the consent, grades the quality, takes the next free storage position automatically and stores the sample, released only when the consent is active and the quality allows it, else quarantined. The 400 is an empty or non-object body, an organization pick the create rule refuses, or a matched participant with no identifier to check its consent against. The 409 is no storage box with free capacity and a free position. The 422 is a legacy alias of a canonical field, or a failed canonical.v1.intake check, with fields and details; or a specimen.quantity at or below zero (INVALID_QUANTITY, with fields and details), refused before anything is written; or boxes with room, none of them in a ready freezer with an operational sensor (success false, error and details). The 403 also comes from a caller with no organization, and the 404 is a picked organization that does not exist. The 503 comes from authenticate and from the handler. Any other failure answers the statusCode it carries, else 500.

409.description: No storage box has free capacity and a free position.

422.description: A non-canonical or invalid field, or no box with room sits in a ready freezer with an operational sensor.

get.summary: Look up the participant an intake would match
get.description: Gates: authenticate, requirePermission('createSample'), requireOrganizationScope (intakeGovernanceResponseGuard rewrites only a POST). It looks the participant up by patientID (or patientId), else by patientName (or name) with birthDate, the name compared without accents, case or repeated spaces, on the day of birth. A participant outside the caller's organizations answers as no match (matched false, patient null), so the lookup reveals neither its fields nor its existence. The 400 is neither a patientID nor both a patientName and a readable birthDate. The 503 comes from authenticate and from the handler, and a lookup failure is 500.

IntakeWizardInput.description: A non-empty object checked against canonical.v1.intake. A legacy alias (patientID, patientId, pseudoId or mongoPatientId in participant; sampleID, sampleId, specimenID, mongoSampleId, parentSampleId, parentSpecimenId, registerDate, registrationDate, withdrawalDate, receivedTime, currentStatus, lifecycleStatus, tcle_id, tcle_template_id, selected_tcle, merkle_root or legacy_compat in specimen; tcle_id, tcle_template_id or selected_tcle in consent; clinical_data, pharmacology_data or biomarkers_values in clinical) answers 422.

participant.description: The participant to match by its identity, or to create.

specimen.description: The specimen; collectionSite (ELM-0128) is kept when given, else the resolved organization.

organizationId.description: The organization the intake is stamped with, picked by the rule POST /api/samples uses: a single-organization caller's own, a multi-organization caller's pick among its own, or a global caller's pick of any existing organization or none.

governanceEvidence.description: RNF018 AC5: governance evidence references, in the shape POST /api/quality/preview takes (optional arrays traceability, monitoring and documentation, at most 20 each, of { uri, hash }). Each presented reference is resolved against the stored record before the intake certifies the specimen; one with a missing hash, an unresolvable URI or a different stored hash fails its category's governance rule, and the specimen is stored quarantined (QUALITY_GOVERNANCE_FAILURE). A custody-event or telemetry reference cannot resolve at intake, since the specimen does not exist yet. A documentation reference resolves only to an approval of specimen.collectionId. Absent evidence leaves its criterion unread. A governanceEvidenceResolution in the body is refused as a non-canonical field.

IntakeWizardResult.description: The body intakeGovernanceResponseGuard rebuilds from the handler's success body; nothing else of it is passed on.

message.description: Says whether the sample is released or stays blocked, and why.

storageLocation.description: The automatically assigned position: equipmentID, boxId, boxName, position and readable.

sample.description: A summary of the stored sample (_id, specimenId, barcode, status, currentStatus, specimenStatus, quarantineReason, final_grade, rcs_score, sprec and its storage location), its governance status read back from the stored sample.

IntakeWizardNonCanonical.description: A non-canonical or invalid field; no success key.

BadRequest.description: Invalid or missing input, or the operation failed.

Unauthorized.description: No, invalid or expired token or session, or an inactive account; on login, refused credentials.

Forbidden.description: Access denied: the permission or role gate refused, the role assignment expired, or MFA setup is pending.

UnprocessableEntity.description: Validation failed; details lists each reason.
